headline: 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi breaks Sachin Tendulkar's record as India's youngest debutant
summary: The batting prodigy made his international debut against England in Manchester, surpassing a milestone held by the legendary Sachin Tendulkar since 1989.
details: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi became the youngest player to represent India after receiving his maiden international cap ahead of a T20 International against England in Manchester.
At 15 years and 99 days, the left-handed batter has now become India's youngest international cricketer, eclipsing Sachin Tendulkar's long-standing record.
Tendulkar was 16 when he made his international debut in a test match against Pakistan in Karachi in November 1989.
Sooryavanshi's rise has been meteoric, including a 35-ball century in the IPL last year and finishing as this year's leading run-scorer with 72 sixes.
India captain Shreyas Iyer backed the teenager, stating that Sooryavanshi is unflinching and completely deserves his place in the squad.
England captain Harry Brook noted that his team had done their homework on the young threat and had prepared specific tactical decisions for the match.
caption:
At just 15 years and 99 days, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has just rewritten the history books of Indian cricket.

Vaibhav Sooryavanshi became the youngest player to represent India after receiving his maiden international cap ahead of a T20 International against England in Manchester.

At 15 years and 99 days, the left-handed batter has now become India's youngest international cricketer, eclipsing Sachin Tendulkar's long-standing record.

Tendulkar was 16 when he made his international debut in a test match against Pakistan in Karachi in November 1989.

Sooryavanshi's rise has been meteoric, including a 35-ball century in the IPL last year and finishing as this year's leading run-scorer with 72 sixes.

India captain Shreyas Iyer backed the teenager, stating that Sooryavanshi is unflinching and completely deserves his place in the squad.

England captain Harry Brook noted that his team had done their homework on the young threat and had prepared specific tactical decisions for the match.

headline_marked: PM Tarique Rahman orders [[reopening of closed state-owned factories]]
headline: PM Tarique Rahman orders reopening of closed state-owned factories
summary: The Prime Minister has directed authorities to expedite the process of reviving loss-making industrial units through local and foreign investment.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has directed authorities to expedite the process of reopening closed and unprofitable state-owned mills and factories.
The revival of these industrial units is planned to be carried out through both local and foreign investment.
During a review meeting at the Prime Minister's Office, the PM emphasized that the entire process must be transparent and completed without unnecessary delays.
The meeting revealed that several private companies have already expressed interest in investing in these closed industrial units.
The government will now assess the feasibility of the proposals submitted by these companies before taking further steps.
The meeting was attended by senior officials, including the Commerce, Industries, and Jute and Textiles Minister, as well as the Finance and Planning Adviser.
caption:
Closed state-owned factories are set for a revival. PM Tarique Rahman has ordered a faster process to reopen them using local and foreign investment.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has directed authorities to expedite the process of reopening closed and unprofitable state-owned mills and factories.

The revival of these industrial units is planned to be carried out through both local and foreign investment.

During a review meeting at the Prime Minister's Office, the PM emphasized that the entire process must be transparent and completed without unnecessary delays.

The meeting revealed that several private companies have already expressed interest in investing in these closed industrial units.

The government will now assess the feasibility of the proposals submitted by these companies before taking further steps.

The meeting was attended by senior officials, including the Commerce, Industries, and Jute and Textiles Minister, as well as the Finance and Planning Adviser.
